text.p: Alexei Akatiev achieved a golden long-distance double with a crushing victory in the men's 25 kilometres river race for Russia to end Sunday with nine of the first 12 titles at the European swimming championships.

Akatiev, who retained his five-km crown by just seven seconds on Friday, left his rivals for dead in the final stages of the longer race in the River Guadalquivir to win the 25 kms by more than 3-1/2 minutes.

Stephane Lecat of France and defending champion Christoph Wandratsch of Germany clasped hands as they swam to the finish to ensure they touched together and shared silver medals after giving up their hopeless pursuit of the Russian, who won in exactly five hours and five minutes.

Russia collected two more golds across town in the San Pablo pools. They completed a sweep of the three synchronised swimming titles with victory in the team event and then Yulia Pakhalina upstaged defending champion Vera Ilyina in the women's three-metre springboard diving final.

Germany's Peggy Buechse ensured the last of the day's golds eluded the Russians when she avenged the loss of her 25-km title by winning the women's five-km event, the last of the long-distance races in Seville.

Buechse touched just ahead of Italy's Valeria Casprini after a protracted sprint duel to the finish, shedding tears after she was eventually confirmed the winner by just one second in one hour and 51 seconds.
Casprini, who led for most of Friday's 25-km event before she was overtaken by Hungary's Rita Kovacs, had to settle for her second Seville silver.
Kovacs, who had toppled Buechse as 25-km champion, found the tables turned when the German passed her in the later stages of the race and took the Hungarian's five-km crown.
Kovacs finished with the bronze in 1:01:06. "I'm tired. The 25 (km) is still in my arms," she said.
Akatiev brooked no challenge to his ambitions in the men's 25 kms.
"When Akatiev left I couldn't follow. I didn't even try. He was too strong," Lecat said.
Inside the last kilometre, with nearest challenger Claudio Gargaro of Italy safely behind, he and Wandratsch agreed to settle for shares of silver.
"We smiled and said 'okay, together'," Lecat said.
Pakhalina, silver medallist behind Ilyina at the 1995 European championships, handed her compatriot a comprehensive defeat on the three-metre springboard.
Pakhalina amassed 567.30 points from the day's 10 dives, leaving Ilyina with the silver (524.28) and Sweden's Anna Lindberg with the bronze (508.02).
It denied Ilyina, the world championship silver medallist, a second successive sweep of the European one-metre and three-metre springboard titles.
